request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the

claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollup audit lines are in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec on the first run.

**How it works:** a new server class, `rollup/Rollup.java`, reads the sheet's figures the way the screen shows them: each person's claimed and due-total (including `n/a`), plus the sheet's two totals. Every change records these figures before it touches anything. After the change's own audit line, it compares them again and writes:
- a `ROLLUP` line for each person whose figures moved, or who is new, in the order people were added;
- then a `TOTALS` line if the sheet's claimed-total or due-total moved.

A change that moves no figure adds no line.

**Where it applies:** adding and editing a person, setting a rate, adding and editing a claim, opening, settling and voiding a claim, taking a statement, and changing the sheet's today. Changing today still has no audit line of its own; it only gets these lines when figures move.

**Things to know:**
- **Changing today now needs the signed-in user.** The server didn't previously ask who changed today, but the new lines need a `by=` name. The endpoint now requires the `X-User` header. The front end already sends it on every request, so nothing in the UI changed.
- **The due-figure rule now exists twice.** `Rollup` has its own copy of the rule for a claim's due figure (settled, then stated, then the live rate on the claim's date) as well as the one in `ClaimService.figure`. I did this so it can work out the whole sheet from one read of the rates. If that rule ever changes, both copies need updating.

No front-end or database schema changes were needed.
